title: workload-opti-settings-memo
content:
Status: DRAFT (notes + quick recommendations for the Optimize team)

Overview
This memo captures workload-specific suggested defaults for batching, prefix/KV caching, and quantization profiles tied back to the 2025 cost model spreadsheet (link above). Purpose is to give product + runtime quick, deployable knobs we can A/B and then bake into Optimize's recommendation engine. This is intentionally pragmatic: conservative defaults first, then workload-specific aggressions once we validate quality impact.

Context and constraints
- We want to reduce per-token cost while preserving latency SLAs for latency-sensitive apps and preserving output quality.
- We have three representative workload buckets used across customer telemetry and interviews:
  1) Low-latency chat (LLC): avg req tokens 20-80, tail reqs < 300, strict p95 latency <= 250ms on dedicated tier.
  2) High-throughput generation (HTG): long-form batching, avg req tokens 400-1,500, latency tolerant (seconds), throughput-oriented.
  3) Embeddings / semantic search (EMB): many small calls (avg tokens 8-64), extremely high QPS and strong cost sensitivity.

Quick summary of recommended defaults (conservative, safe)
- LLC (chat): batching: max_batch_tokens=6k, max_batch_age=12ms, prefer adaptive small batches; caching: prefix caching ON for stable prompts, KV cache TTL=30m for user session keys; quant: conservative int8 (GPTQ disabled) for 7B/13B variants; expected cost reduction ~18–22% vs baseline (fp16) with p95 latency change <8%.
- HTG (high-throughput gen): batching: max_batch_tokens=64k, max_batch_age=60ms, enable background batching + async flush thresholds; caching: prefix caching ON for repeated prompt templates with TTL=6h; quant: aggressive int4-GPTQ for 13B+/70B where validated; expected cost reduction ~35–55% with slight quality checks required.
- EMB (embeddings): batching: batch-bytes threshold enabled, max_batch_size=2048 requests, max_batch_age=40ms; caching: result-level cache + semantic dedupe for identical inputs (TTL=24h), KV cache disabled (not useful); quant: int8 or int4 depending on vector similarity tests; expected cost reduction ~28–40%.

Detailed rationale and microbench numbers (from cost model sheet)
- Benchmarks used: per-model token/sec from runtime perf runs (sheet: per_model_microbench tab). Representative numbers (median across 8 GPU types):
  - Llama2-13B fp16: 320 tok/s single stream, int8: +1.6x effective, int4-GPTQ: +2.8x effective (quality dependent).
  - Falcon-40B fp16: 460 tok/s baseline; int8: +1.25x; int4: risky — use only with eval set.
- Cost model assumptions: GPU price/second normalized (sheet handles region multipliers), per-request orchestration overhead (avg 4.5ms), network overhead for small requests accounted for separately.

Specific recommended settings (table as bullets)
- Batching knobs (runtime config keys)
  - batch.max_batch_tokens: LLC=6_000, HTG=64_000, EMB=32_000
  - batch.max_batch_age_ms: LLC=12, HTG=60, EMB=40
  - batch.max_concurrent_streams_per_worker: LLC=16, HTG=4, EMB=24
  - batch.concurrent_mode: LLC="adaptive_small", HTG="background_merge", EMB="request_size_aware"

- Caching knobs
  - cache.prefix_enabled: LLC=true, HTG=true, EMB=false
  - cache.kv_ttl_seconds: LLC=1800 (30m), HTG=21600 (6h), EMB=0
  - cache.max_memory_percent_per_pod: LLC=10%, HTG=18%, EMB=6%
  - cache.dedupe_threshold: EMB=0.98 similarity for immediate cache hit

- Quantization profiles (names correspond to Optimize UI):
  - q_profile.conservative_int8: description="safest int8 path (per-layer calibration)", recommended_for=["LLC", "EMB"], profile_name="int8-safe-v1"
  - q_profile.aggressive_int4_gptq: description="GPTQ int4 with per-layer block size=128, groups=1", recommended_for=["HTG"], profile_name="gptq-int4-128-v1"
  - q_profile.mixed_precision: description="fp16 for key layers + int8 elsewhere", recommended_for=["LLC","HTG"]

Expected tradeoffs and risk matrix
- Latency-sensitive risk: Increasing batch_age or batch size increases p95 tail — we must enforce route-level SLOs and reject recommendations on routes with p95 < configured threshold.
- Quality risk: int4-GPTQ can produce hallucination regressions on some instruction-tuned models. Mandatory: run a 500+ example differential eval (sheet: eval_runs tab) before enabling automatic rollout.
- Operational risk: KV cache churn when many short-lived sessions — keep default TTL conservative (30m) and build a cache-hit dashboard to monitor 95th percentile miss rate per route.

Experiment matrix (small, medium, wide)
- Small (1 week): LLC aggressive batch_age 20ms -> observe p95 latency, token cost delta. Metric: p95 latency, cost per 1k tokens, error-rate. Owner: Ravi Shah.
- Medium (2–3 weeks): HTG enable int4-GPTQ on staging for 4 customers (bounded rollback). Metric: generation quality score (BLEU/ROUGE or downstream metric), cost savings. Owner: Sofia Carter.
- Wide (4+ weeks): Auto-recommendation rollout: surface suggested profile in Console; enable one-click apply with A/B 50/50 and automatic rollback on quality alarms. Owner: Marco Diaz.

Telemetry and dashboards to build
- Optimize UI: per-route expected savings estimate (from cost model) + fidelity score.
- SLI dashboards: cache_hit_rate (p50/p95), avg_batch_size, batch_age_ms distribution, quantization_quality_regression (user-specified metric), cost_per_1k_tokens by model.

Open questions / notes to self
- How to automatically classify routes into LLC/HTG/EMB? Propose a lightweight classifier: features = avg_request_tokens, median_inter_arrival_ms, 90th_percentile_tokens. We'll prototype in product-ops.
- Need a canonical small eval set per model for GPTQ testing. Who curates? Suggest research/aml owns the seed sets.
- Pricing UX: show estimated monthly $ savings and a confidence band (low/expected/high) taken from the cost model uncertainty column.

Action items / next steps
- [Ava] Push the conservative defaults to a feature-flagged runtime build (optimize/ff/quick-batch-defaults). Link PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/1284
- [Ravi] Run LLC small experiment across 6 internal customers (Jan 20–27). Report metrics.
- [Sofia] Run GPTQ quality sweep on Llama2-13B and Falcon-40B, publish evaluation artifacts to /optimize/evals/gptq-jan25.
- [Marco] Wire up the cost-model delta numbers into the Console prototype (estimate card).

Appendix: quick checklist before rollout
- Regression eval >= 500 examples per model variant
- Observability: dashboard with live traffic, auto-alert on p95 latency increase > 10% or quality regression above threshold
- Opt-out controls: per-customer, per-route toggle to disable recommendations

Notes: rough draft — keep iterative details here.
Unresolved: embedding dedupe rate threshold; need to validate on real corpus sizes (sheet: embed_lookups tab).

If this looks ok I will convert to a Confluence page and create OPT JIRA epic.

End of memo
